gist: A domestic violence survivor lives in fear after her attacker was released without a tracking tag.
A watchdog report reveals nearly half of offenders are not tagged promptly upon prison release.
Prison officers propose training staff to fit electronic tags before offenders leave prison.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A domestic violence survivor named Michelle is living in terror after her former partner was released from prison without a GPS tracking tag. Despite previous probation breaches and threats of violence, the monitoring device was not fitted.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Delays in fitting electronic tags leave high-risk domestic abuse survivors vulnerable and forced to alter their lives completely. A watchdog report revealed that tagging contractors met performance targets merely by attempting to fit devices rather than ensuring they worked.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The prison officers union has suggested training prison staff to fit tags before inmates leave prison. Meanwhile, the government stated it is expanding electronic monitoring and tagging offenders before release.

articles.title: Zverev becomes deserved world number one - but sense of discomfort remains
articles.standfirst: Alexander Zverev has been the best player in the world in men's tennis this year - but a sense of discomfort remains.

gist: Alexander Zverev will end 2026 as a two-time major champion and world number one.
He won the French Open and US Open after changing his on-court approach.
Zverev has previously faced accusations of physical abuse and a German court penalty.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Alexander Zverev won the French Open and US Open, becoming the oldest man in over 50 years to reach world number one for the first time. His success followed ten days spent with Rafael and Toni Nadal in Mallorca. Despite his on-court achievements, Zverev remains a polarising figure due to past allegations of physical abuse from two former partners, an ATP investigation, and a German court penalty order.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Zverev has transformed from being considered the best male player without a Grand Slam title into a dominant two-time major champion. However, a sense of discomfort remains around his status at the top of the sport given the serious allegations made against him and the public scrutiny he continues to face.
